title: LIV Golf Finds a Mystery Investor to Save the League After Saudi Money Dries Up
summary: Have you ever had to find a new teammate when someone quit the game? That's what LIV Golf just did! The golf league, which started in 2022 with billions of dollars from Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF), was in big trouble. The PIF said in April it would stop funding LIV at the end of 2026. That meant the league might have to cancel events or even go bankrupt. But on Wednesday, LIV's CEO Scott O'Neil announced they've found a new 'lead investor'—but they won't say who it is yet! The deal is expected to close in September. Even cooler: the players will become the majority owners of the league. That's never happened before in a major global sports league. O'Neil says more than a dozen other groups might also invest smaller amounts. LIV Golf had to cancel its New Orleans event and its season-ending championship. Now, they plan to return next season with 10 events—half in the U.S. and half around the world. This weekend, they're playing at former President Trump's golf club in New Jersey. It's a big turnaround for a league that many thought was finished.
why_it_matters: This shows that even big sports leagues can run out of money and need to find clever solutions—like when your team loses a player and you have to quickly find a new one to keep playing.

background_read: LIV Golf started in 2022 as a new league to compete with the traditional PGA Tour, offering huge prizes to attract top golfers.
It was paid for by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, which many people criticized—they thought Saudi Arabia was using sports to improve its reputation.
When the Saudi money is set to end in 2026, finding a secret new investor was a surprise that might keep the league alive.
Article_Structure: WHO: LIV Golf's CEO Scott O'Neil and a mystery 'lead investor' (with players becoming majority owners).
WHAT: A new, unnamed investor will save the league from going bankrupt after Saudi Arabia's PIF stops its funding.
WHERE: The announcement happened while LIV is playing at former President Trump's golf club in New Jersey, but the league operates globally.
WHY: Without new money, LIV would have to cancel events; the league needed a rescue to continue beyond 2026 and keep its schedule running.

perspectives.description: They are relieved and excited that the league won't disappear, and think giving players real ownership is a groundbreaking, fair idea.
They question why the new investor is a secret, and worry that the money might not be enough or could come with hidden agendas.
They see this as a risky experiment, but note that if it works, player-owned leagues could change how professional sports are run in the future.
